problem: Transformer-based VLN agents use dedicated history encoders (LSTM, memory graphs, hierarchical transformer encoders) to record past observations and actions, which raises model complexity and compute. Their training also mixes many pre-training proxy tasks and combines IL and RL with static weights, which is hard to balance.
motivation: VLN needs the agent to keep track of a changing visual context over time, but explicit history modules are costly. A decoder-only sequence model can read history straight from the trajectory sequence. Separating exploitation (offline imitation) from exploration (online RL fine-tuning) should also simplify training.
key_idea: Treat VLN as Decision-Transformer-style sequential decision making, using a GPT-2 decoder over (return, state, action) trajectories with no history encoder, trained by offline single-step action prediction and then online fine-tuning with a policy-entropy exploration objective.
insight: Conditioning on the trajectory sequence matters: limiting history length to 1 drops val-unseen SR from 65.14 to 58.65 and SPL from 61.09 to 53.42. Both training stages are needed: PT only gives 52.34 SR and FT only gives 64.76 SR on val-unseen, versus 65.14 with both. Decoder choice (OPT/Llama/GPT), language-pretrained GPT-2 weights and depth beyond 12 layers make little difference, so the sequence formulation, not the specific LLM, drives the gains. The data is too small to benefit from larger models.
method: Sequential formulation: the trajectory is (r,s,a) tokens as in the Decision Transformer, and the policy conditions on the full trajectory history, so history is implicit and no history encoder is needed.
Input encoding: instruction encoded by a pretrained Sentence-BERT ([CLS], 768-d); each of the 36 panoramic views encoded by a pretrained ViT (768-d, HAMT settings).
Modality fusion: element-wise product of the instruction [CLS] embedding and each view embedding gives the state s_{t,i}, replacing a cross-modal transformer.
VLN-GPT decoder: GPT-2 base (12 layers) with masked attention over return/state/action embeddings plus a time-step embedding (instead of positional encoding), and a linear output layer.
Offline pre-training: sequence action prediction (SAP) only, with a 2-layer FC head over navigable views (as in HAMT) and cross-entropy on expert actions; 50k iterations, lr 5e-5, batch 64.
Online fine-tuning: RL with a policy-entropy term for exploration, following the Online Decision Transformer; 100k iterations, lr 1e-5, batch 8.

setting.backbone: GPT-2 base decoder (trained from scratch by default) + Sentence-BERT text encoder + ViT image encoder (pretrained)
setting.training_data: R2R only (offline expert trajectories for pre-training, then online interaction on R2R); no extra or synthetic data

results: On R2R, VLN-GPT reaches val-unseen SR 65 / SPL 61 / NE 3.75 and val-seen SR 76 / SPL 72 / NE 2.55, beating the strongest baseline RecBERT (val-unseen SR 63 / SPL 57 / NE 3.93). It also gets higher SAP accuracy in pre-training than HAMT (72 vs 68 on val-unseen).
limitations: Evaluated on R2R only; the model does not benefit from more parameters on small VLN datasets, and longer trajectories and more complex instructions are unexplored.
